environment.scope: Native Linux x86_64 development evidence: scoped task context, candidate coverage, stale queue refusal, native Xvfb scope UI with capability-negotiated PNG evidence through the scripted ACP peer, and preset snapshot render/relocation using a locally assembled managed SDK from this checkout without an overlay. No authenticated provider, physical display/audio, Windows or macOS claim.

dev_scoped_task_context.criteria: Scope packet round-trip, half-open selection semantics, source identity checks, and preservation of the frozen task scope through candidate capture pass their focused studio-engine tests.
dev_scoped_task_context.notes: Six scope tests and the 32-test candidate-validation suite passed, including bounded scene-source matching, source-hash verification, and candidate scope retention. This is development-fixture evidence, not a provider or preset qualification.

dev_scoped_candidate_coverage.criteria: Selected half-open range samples and adjacent boundaries are inspected and rendered; a candidate shorter than its frozen range is retained as incomplete.
dev_scoped_candidate_coverage.notes: The focused candidate-validation tests passed for requested sample coverage and fail-closed shortened-candidate coverage.

dev_stale_queue_refusal.criteria: A queued scope becomes visibly stale when the displayed preview identity changes and is refused without launching a second writer.
dev_stale_queue_refusal.notes: The focused AgentWorkflow scripted-peer integration test passed. The peer proves application workflow behavior only.

dev_native_linux_scope_ui.criteria: The Linux native shell displays a pending frozen scope and actual before/candidate evidence without fabricating preview pixels; representative states are inspected through the running UI.
dev_native_linux_scope_ui.notes: The native M4 Xvfb shell test passes: scene/range scope, revision-matched before/after evidence, capability-negotiated bounded PNG image blocks, and stale queued-scope refusal. The default AutoApply range path exposes decoded before/after thumbnails in its terminal task snapshot, and ManualReview still exposes its review controls. The M3 apply/Undo native regression also passes separately. The peer is scripted, not an authentic provider.

dev_managed_sdk_preset_render.criteria: A generated project renders the same token-bound source from two portable preset snapshots and survives relocation/reopen.
dev_managed_sdk_preset_render.notes: Pass on a locally assembled native managed SDK from this checkout: its SDK id is recorded, fframes::Styles is present, and the relocation script ran directly against the SDK without taking its overlay branch. This is Linux development evidence, not a published SDK release or cross-platform/provider qualification.

auth_provider_scoped_edit.criteria: A real authenticated ACP provider completes a scoped edit with revision-matched baseline/candidate evidence and safe teardown.
auth_provider_scoped_edit.notes: No authentic scoped edit was attempted; scripted fixtures and adapter readiness probes are not substitutes.
auth_provider_scoped_edit.prerequisite: Use an operator-authenticated real ACP adapter and run the scoped edit, review and teardown sequence on the managed SDK.

auth_windows.criteria: The complete M4 workflow is exercised on Windows, including native interaction and task/process cleanup.
auth_windows.notes: Windows development evidence now exists (m0-results.json additional_platforms, evidence/windows-m0-2026-10-11): the desktop workspace suite passes on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and the packaged app installs the managed SDK, compiles a worker and presents frames with native input on a Windows Server 2022 VM. The M4 scoped workflow itself was not run there because no authenticated provider was available.
auth_windows.prerequisite: Run the complete M4 qualification on a Windows host with a compatible SDK, native shell and an authenticated provider.

auth_macos.criteria: The complete M4 workflow is exercised on macOS, including native interaction and task/process cleanup.
auth_macos.notes: No macOS host was available for this run.
auth_macos.prerequisite: Run the complete M4 qualification on a macOS host with a compatible SDK and native shell.

acceptance.reason: M4 development gates pass on native Linux x86_64, including a locally assembled managed SDK with fframes::Styles. Full M4 qualification remains not_run because authenticated-provider, Windows and macOS gates are not_run.
